transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Ellis (Stonegate CISO), Rina Patel (Head of Cloud Security), Omar Diaz (Platform Eng), Leah Kim (Compliance), Ben Foster (Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO, audit logs, data retention policy, SOC 2 artifacts and next steps for pilot. Agreed to share SOC2, audit-log schema, and retention confirmation. Agreed follow-up 4/28 to validate RBAC mapping and log ingestion.

Topics: SSO/SAML integration, audit log schema and retention, SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM and key management, RBAC and user provisioning, data residency for pilot, dedicated vs hosted concerns

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call
- uh Jordan from Redwood here, Priya's with me, and, Mark, Rina, Omar, Leah, Ben from Stonegate, thanks for making the time.
[00:12] Mark: Yep thanks, Jordan. We only have 45 so let's try to be tight. Main things for us this week are SOC two artifacts and the audit log detail, plus SSO progress.
[00:22] Priya: Cool, I'll start with audit logs and retention notes, happy to clarify as we go.
[00:30] Rina: Quick note
- legal has been explicit we can't keep full transcripts longer than 90 days for the pilot unless fields are masked; we need a clear retention policy and proof of deletion for demo data.
[00:42] Jordan: Understood. That's consistent with what we heard last week. We have configurable retention controls at route level, and you can set automatic purges; we'll share the UI and API calls.
[00:54] Priya: For logs
- our runtime emits an append-only audit log with events: request meta, user id (if available), model id, timestamp, and a hashed user identifier. We also include action types and response status. We can export logs to S3 or to your SIEM via Kinesis/Kafka.
[01:10] Omar: Is the user id plain text? We need to avoid PII.
[01:13] Priya: Good q
- by default we hash user identifiers with a per-customer salt. For pilot we can also anonymize and strip free-text fields. There's an option to mask token-level outputs as well.
[01:25] Leah: When you say hashed with per-customer salt
- who holds the salt? Is that in your KMS?
[01:29] Priya: Salt is customer-specific and managed in your KMS if you use our KMS integration; if not, we store it in a HSM-backed key store. We can provide diagrams.
[01:38] Mark: We need to see the KMS integration flow and proof of encryption at rest for the logs. SOC two evidence.
[01:44] Jordan: Yeah we'll attach the SOC2 Type II report and encryption diagrams. Expect that in the drop I'm sending on Friday.
[01:51] Ben: One practical ask
- can you show the audit log schema? Our SIEM team wants fields mapped to our internal taxonomy.
[01:58] Priya: Sure. I'll export a schema sample
- JSON lines
- and a sample 24-hour export obfuscated. We'll include field descriptions: event_type, request_id, model_version, latency_ms, user_hash, route, retention_ttl.
[02:14] Omar: For retention TTL, do you support TTL per-route? We want longer retention for admin audit events and shorter for user-facing transcript content.
[02:21] Priya: Yes configurable per route. You can set TTL in days and we have immediate deletion API for manual purges. Deletion is irreversible and we log deletion events.
[02:31] Mark: How's access control to those logs? RBAC?
[02:35] Priya: RBAC is via SCIM and roles mapped from your IdP. We support SAML and OIDC for SSO, SCIM provisioning for groups. Logs are stored in a customer-owned S3 bucket if you choose, and we can lock down access via IAM roles.
[02:47] Rina: Are you saying the logs can be stored in our S3? We prefer that for compliance.
[02:50] Jordan: Yes you can sink audit logs into your S3 bucket. For the hosted pilot route we also keep a copy for operational reasons but can disable long-term retention. We'll document that.
[03:02] Leah: SOC two question
- do you have a list of control mappings and evidence artifacts you can hand us?
[03:08] Jordan: We have a SOC2 evidence pack and a control mapping doc. I will share the SOC2 Type II report and a controls-to-evidence spreadsheet.
[03:16] Priya: And two quick technical notes
- we support envelope encryption and KMS integration for model weights and for logs. If you need HSM-backed key storage, we have an optional HSM integration.
[03:27] Omar: For the pilot, we want to run a small benchmark against a dedicated pool with RBAC enabled so we can validate audit logging end-to-end. Can Redwood spin that up?
[03:36] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated pilot nodes we can provision a short-lived pool. We'll need a capacity window and model pinned. Jordan, you want to coordinate?
[03:42] Jordan: Yep I'll get an estimate and schedule. We'll also include instructions to authenticate via SSO and SCIM mapping so your users are provisioned correctly during the test.
[03:51] Ben: About SSO
- last week we started SAML metadata exchange. Where do we stand?
[03:55] Rina: We uploaded metadata but saw a mapping mismatch on groups.
[03:59] Priya: That usually is claim mapping
- we'll send sample Attribute Statements for groups, email, and role. For SCIM, group sync should map to our role names: admin, auditor, developer.
[04:10] Rina: We need an "auditor" role that only reads logs, can't call the API.
[04:14] Priya: That's supported
- read-only auditor role that has access to logs and dashboards but no generator tokens.
[04:20] Mark: Any concerns about data residency? Our legal wants EU only storage for EU customers, pilot includes EU test tenants.
[04:27] Jordan: We can route EU requests through EU regions; for pilot you'll want to pin the region and the log sink. We'll confirm region pins in the runbook we share.
[04:36] Leah: A quick compliance nuance
- we need evidence of deletion for any purge requests within 48 hours. Is that doable?
[04:42] Priya: Deletion events are auditable and we can emit a signed deletion receipt. We'll include that in the audit export sample.
[04:50] Omar: On retention, if legal requires redaction rather than deletion, can you redact content?
[04:55] Priya: Yes we support automated redaction of PII fields and also an on-demand redaction API for stored objects.
[05:02] Jordan: Recap: Jordan will send SOC2 and pen test, Priya will send audit log schema and sample export, Priya will also share SAML claim mapping docs, Omar will confirm retention windows with legal, Leah will send compliance stakeholder list. Follow-up on 2026-04-28 to validate RBAC mapping and test the dedicated pool.
[05:18] Mark: Sounds good. Also, any competitive notes
- we looked at AcmeAI and LambdaServe; main differentiator for Redwood is the unified runtime and the per-route retention controls. Keep showing that.
[05:30] Priya: Got it. We'll prepare the artifact bundle and a short runbook for the RBAC and SSO flows.
[05:36] Jordan: Any final q's?
[05:38] Leah: Just confirm you can provide the signed deletion receipts within 48 hours of a purge?
[05:42] Priya: Yes. We'll add that to the runbook.
[05:45] Jordan: Thanks everyone
- we'll follow up with the artifacts and I'll create the calendar invite for 4/28.

End of transcript.

References / Shared artifacts:
- SOC2_Type_II_Stonegate_Request.pdf (will be shared via secure box)
- Audit_log_schema_sample.jsonl (sample exported, obfuscated)
- SAML_attribute_mapping_example.txt
- Dedicated_pool_runbook_and_capacity_estimate.xlsx

Action recap (auto): Jordan to share SOC2 & pen test; Priya to share audit log sample and SAML mapping; Omar/Leah to confirm retention/legal. Follow-up 2026-04-28 to validate RBAC and run dedicated benchmark.
